clinician.final_diagnosis: Pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma of the adult bladder
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old Chinese male presented with 10 days of intermittent gross hematuria. Initial B ultrasound revealed hypoechoic nodules in the right upper bladder wall. Cystoscopy demonstrated a 3.0×3.0 cm globular mass with a narrow pedicle and sheet-like yellow calcification on the right anterior wall. Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) was performed; pathology confirmed pleomorphic rhabdomyosarcoma with no residual tumor in the muscularis. Immunohistochemistry showed positive skeletal muscle differentiation markers (MyoD1 positive, myogenin partially positive, vimentin positive) and negative epithelial markers (CK negative, GATA3 negative, SMA negative), with high proliferative activity (Ki-67 45%+) and P53 mutation pattern (90%+). Pre-chemotherapy PET-CT showed no metastatic disease. The patient received adjuvant chemotherapy with intravenous dacarbazine and doxorubicin with good tolerability and no adverse events. Follow-up enhanced CT scans on December 7, 2023, and March 5, 2024, showed no tumor recurrence.
